briefdescription.para: Resets the CAN device.

detaileddescription.para: Calling this function resets the device immediately, and any pending transmission or reception is terminated at once. Both Object Layer and Transfer Layer are reset. This function does not reset the Physical Layer. All registers are reset to the default values, and no previous status is restored. TX FIFO, RX FIFO and TX High Priority Buffer are also reset.

When an internal error requires a reset, the driver notifies the upper layer software through the error status code or interrupts. The upper layer software is responsible for calling this Reset function and then re-configuring the device.
The CAN device is in Configuration Mode immediately after this function returns.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCanFd instance to be worked on.

Any filter not specified in this parameter keeps its previous enable or disable setting. If all acceptance filters are disabled then all received frames are stored in the RX FIFO.

briefdescription.para: Sets values for the Acceptance Filter Mask and ID Registers.

detaileddescription.para: Sets values to the Acceptance Filter Mask Register (AFMR) and Acceptance Filter ID Register (AFIR) for the specified Acceptance Filter. Use XCANFD_IDR_* defined in xcanfd_hw.h to create the values to set the filter. Read xcanfd.h and device specification for details.

This function should be called only after:
The given filter is disabled by calling XCanFd_AcceptFilterDisable().
And the CAN device is ready to accept writes to AFMR and AFIR, that is, XCanFd_IsAcceptFilterBusy() returns FALSE.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCanFd instance to be worked on.
Defines which Acceptance Filter Mask and ID Register to set. Use any single XCANFD_AFR_UAF*_MASK value. Ranges from 1 - 32.
Value to write to the chosen Acceptance Filter Mask Register.
Value to write to the chosen Acceptance Filter ID Register.

simplesect.para:
- XST_SUCCESS if the values were set successfully.
XST_FAILURE if the given filter was not disabled, or the CAN device was not ready to accept writes to AFMR and AFIR.
Acceptance Filter Mask and ID Registers are optional registers in Xilinx XCanFd device. If they are not configured then the device receives data with any ID.

simplesect.para: Acceptance Filter Mask and ID Registers are optional registers in Xilinx CAN device. If they are NOT existing in the device, this function should NOT be used. Calling this function in this case causes an assertion failure.

briefdescription.para: Receives a CAN/CAN FD Frame in sequential mode.

detaileddescription.para: Checks the FSR Register. The FL bits indicate the number of packets received. If FL is non-zero, reads the packet and stores it to the supplied buffer.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCanFd instance to be worked on.
Pointer to a 32-bit aligned buffer where the CAN/CAN FD frame is to be written.

simplesect.para:
- XST_SUCCESS if RX FIFO was not empty and a frame was read from RX FIFO successfully and written into the given buffer.
XST_NO_DATA if there is no frame to be received from the FIFO.

The CANFD has two design modes. ->Sequential Mode - Core writes data sequentially to RxBuffers. ->MailBox Mode - Core writes data to RxBuffers when a ID Match happened. This routine distinguishes receive checking as per the frame availability from either Fifo 0 or Fifo 1.

briefdescription.para: Receives a CAN Frame in Mailbox Mode.

detaileddescription.para: Reads the Rx Last Buffer Index from the ISR Register. This indicates which buffer contains data. Then reads and updates the data to the supplied buffer.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCanFd instance to be worked on.
Pointer to a 32-bit aligned buffer where the CAN frame is to be received.

simplesect.para:
- XST_SUCCESS if RX FIFO was not empty and a frame was read from RX FIFO successfully and written into the given buffer.
XST_NO_DATA if there is no frame to be received from the FIFO.

This CANFD has two design modes. ->Sequential Mode - Core writes data sequentially to RxBuffers. ->MailBox Mode - Core writes data to RxBuffers when a ID match happened. This routine is useful for MailBox Mode.

briefdescription.para: Receives CAN/CAN FD TX Events in sequential mode.

detaileddescription.para: Checks the FSR Register. The FL bits indicate the number of TX Event packets received. If FL is non-zero, reads the packet and stores it to the supplied buffer.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCanFd instance to be worked on.

simplesect.para:
- XST_SUCCESS if TXE FIFO was not empty and a frame was read from TX FIFO successfully and written into the given buffer.
XST_NO_DATA if there is no frame to be received from the TXE FIFO.

This CANFD has two design modes. ->Sequential Mode - Core writes data sequentially to RxBuffers. ->MailBox Mode - Core writes data to RxBuffers when a ID Match happened. This routine is useful for Both the Modes. This API is meant to be used with IP with CanFD 2.0 spec support only.

briefdescription.para: Cancels a CAN/CAN FD Frame transmission request.

detaileddescription.para: Checks the TRR Bit based on BufferNumber. If the TRR Bit is set, cancels the buffer transmission.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCanFd instance to be worked on.
Which Buffer to cancel out of 32 Buffers.

simplesect.para:
- XST_SUCCESS if cancellation was successful.
XST_FAILURE if the buffer has no pending transmission.

This function first checks whether the TRR bit is set.
If it is set, the function checks the corresponding TCR bit.
If the TCR bit is set, the function waits until cancellation is performed.
If the TCR bit is not set, the function sets it and waits until the core clears it.
If the TRR bit is not set, the function does nothing.

briefdescription.para: Runs a self-test on the CAN driver/device.

detaileddescription.para: The test resets the device and sets up the Loop Back mode. It then sends a standard frame, receives the frame, verifies the contents, and resets the device again.
Note that this is a destructive test in that resets of the device are performed. Refer to the device specification for the device status after the reset operation.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCanFd instance to be worked on.

simplesect.para:
- XST_SUCCESS if the self-test passed, that is, the frame received via the internal loop back has the same contents as the sent frame.
XST_FAILURE otherwise.

If the CAN device does not work properly, this function may enter an infinite loop and never returns to the caller.
If XST_FAILURE is returned, the device is not reset so that the caller could have a chance to check the reasons causing the failure.

briefdescription.para: Enables one or more interrupts.

detaileddescription.para: Use the XCANFD_IXR_* constants defined in xcanfd_hw.h to create the bit-mask to enable interrupts.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCanFd instance.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCanFd instance.

briefdescription.para: Handles CAN FD driver interrupts.

detaileddescription.para: Reads the interrupt status from the ISR, determines the source of the interrupts, calls according callbacks, and finally clears the interrupts.

Application beyond this driver is responsible for providing callbacks to handle interrupts and installing the callbacks using XCanFd_SetHandler() during initialization phase. An example delivered with this driver demonstrates how this could be done.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCanFd instance that just interrupted.

briefdescription.para: Installs an asynchronous callback function.

detaileddescription.para: Installs a callback for the given HandlerType:

para.preformatted: HandlerType Callback Function Type ----------------------- --------------------------- XCANFD_HANDLER_SEND XCanFd_SendRecvHandler XCANFD_HANDLER_RECV XCanFd_SendRecvHandler XCANFD_HANDLER_ERROR XCanFd_ErrorHandler XCANFD_HANDLER_EVENT XCanFd_EventHandler

HandlerType Invoked by this driver when: ----------------------- -------------------------------------------------- XCANFD_HANDLER_SEND A frame transmitted by a call to XCanFd_Send() has been sent successfully.
XCANFD_HANDLER_RECV A frame has been received and is sitting in the RX FIFO.
XCANFD_HANDLER_ERROR An error interrupt is occurring.
XCANFD_HANDLER_EVENT Any other kind of interrupt is occurring.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCanFd instance.
Specifies which handler is to be attached.
Address of the callback function.
User data item that is passed to the callback function when it is invoked.

simplesect.para:
- XST_SUCCESS when handler is installed.
XST_INVALID_PARAM when HandlerType is invalid.
Invoking this function for a handler that already has been installed replaces it with the new handler.
